population_anchor.definition: household money income / people in household; person-weighted 30th percentile

pressures.label: U-6 Labor Underutilization Rate
pressures.notes: Total unemployed, plus all marginally attached workers, plus total employed part-time for economic reasons, as a percent of civilian labor force plus marginally attached workers. National Economic Pressure Signal (broad labor force measure, not Bottom-30 specific).

pressures.label: Civilian Labor Force Participation Rate
pressures.notes: Percent of civilian noninstitutional population 16+ working or actively looking for work. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: Employment-Population Ratio
pressures.notes: Proportion of civilian noninstitutional population 16+ currently employed. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: Persons Outside Labor Force Who Want a Job
pressures.notes: Persons not in the labor force who currently report wanting a job. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: CPI-U All Items (Headline Inflation)
pressures.notes: Year-over-year percentage change in headline Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: CPI — Food at Home (Groceries)
pressures.notes: Year-over-year grocery price inflation. High direct impact on lower-income household budgets. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: CPI — Shelter
pressures.notes: Year-over-year residential shelter and rent price inflation. Critical basic necessity component. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: CPI — Medical Care
pressures.notes: Year-over-year healthcare service and prescription drug price inflation. National Economic Pressure Signal.

pressures.label: CPI — Gasoline (All Types)
pressures.notes: Year-over-year retail motor gasoline price change. High-frequency commuting expense signal. National Economic Pressure Signal.

mit_living_wage.author: Dr. Amy Glasmeier / MIT
mit_living_wage.methodological_divergence: MIT includes unsubsidized commercial healthcare, civic engagement, and local county cost aggregation. The Foundation models independent standard housing, USDA Low-Cost food, explicit auto ownership, unsubsidized Silver Marketplace healthcare, and full statutory federal/state taxes.
mit_living_wage.name: MIT Living Wage Calculator

official_poverty_measure.author: U.S. Census Bureau / HHS
official_poverty_measure.methodological_divergence: OPM is based on a 1963 3x food multiplier and severely underestimates modern shelter, transit, healthcare, and utility costs.
official_poverty_measure.name: Official Poverty Measure (OPM)

united_way_alice.author: United Way
united_way_alice.methodological_divergence: ALICE includes a 10% contingency buffer but assumes smaller healthcare and transport baselines. The Foundation models full automobile ownership and unsubsidized Silver health insurance.
united_way_alice.name: United For ALICE Survival Budget
